# Agent Evaluation Requirements Checklist: SmartQ Agent Evaluation

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurable quality of requirements for the SmartQ Agent validation-set collection, scoring, and reporting workflow.  
**Created**: 2026-08-20  
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the required validation-record fields and their invalid-data handling fully specified for every input record? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the configured Agent identity, tenant, authentication, and optional knowledge-base scope requirements fully documented without implying that credentials belong in datasets or artifacts? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the durable per-question result fields sufficient to reconstruct each source question's collection and scoring eligibility without relying on transient Agent state? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the specification distinguish required result evidence for successful, failed, and invalid-response records? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006]

## Requirement Clarity and Consistency

- [ ] CHK005 Is “one at a time” quantified consistently as at most one in-flight Agent request for the full evaluation run? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the expected mapping between SmartQ retrieval references and validation-set chunk identifiers explicitly defined, including index origin and ranking preservation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK007 Are “unusable response,” “failed,” and “unscorable” defined so their meanings do not overlap or conflict across collection, retrieval scoring, and generation scoring? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the scope of “all supported metrics” tied to a documented metric registry or naming convention rather than left open-ended? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK009 Do the success criteria define an objective observable condition for preserving source order and limiting Agent request concurrency? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK010 Do the success criteria define the expected deterministic inputs and comparison basis for every requested retrieval and generation metric? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the report traceability criterion precise about which per-question evidence must be sufficient to explain successful, failed, and unscorable outcomes? [Clarity, Spec §SC-003, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK012 Is re-scoring reproducibility defined with stable artifact identity and an explicit boundary for configuration or metric-selection changes? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]

## Scenario and Edge-case Coverage

- [ ] CHK013 Are primary collection requirements complete for a validation set with more than one question, including source-order preservation and terminal accounting? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1]
- [ ] CHK014 Are requirements specified for partial collection interruption or local write failure, including how an incomplete run is identified and protected from accidental scoring? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements specified for an Agent response with references that omit, duplicate, reorder, or use a non-compatible chunk identifier? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK016 Are zero eligible records and mixed eligibility across retrieval and generation explicitly addressed for every aggregate metric? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK017 Are output-directory collision and explicit replacement/resume semantics mutually consistent with the requirement that existing partial records remain auditable? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Security, Privacy, and Dependencies

- [ ] CHK018 Are credential-redaction requirements specific enough to cover final answers, SSE diagnostics, errors, run metadata, reports, and command-line output? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK019 Are the assumptions about SmartQ’s session-backed Agent interface, returned answer form, and retrieval-reference shape documented as externally validated dependencies? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the retention boundary for private raw Agent content and local evaluation artifacts specified beyond the prohibition on committing credentials? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK021 Are timeout, retry, and service-unavailability requirements defined consistently enough to distinguish an individual failed record from a run-level preflight failure? [Gap, Spec §FR-006, §Edge Cases]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- This checklist evaluates the written requirements, not implementation behavior.
